changes.old_value: Comparison is the mind's most fundamental operation for making the unfamiliar intelligible. When we encounter something new, we reach for something known—we say it is LIKE this, UNLIKE that, MORE than one thing, LESS than another. This analogical impulse is not merely pedagogical convenience; it is constitutive of reasoning itself. Every classification, every evaluation, every argument about degree or kind relies on implicit or explicit comparison. Yet precisely because comparison is so ubiquito...
changes.new_value: A compact audit ordered by the conclusions that depend on comparison: what is transferred, which correspondence warrants it, where disanalogies matter, and what weaker conclusion survives. The desks lift comparison → conclusion → correspondence → defeating difference → scoped verdict, plus criteria and alternatives. The reading’s categories are the consequential comparisons in this text. A text making comparisons; source and target material when the comparison relies on facts outside it.
